body: BLOCK exact 63deb2a9fcf52ae2e981c22d97f581e7c760257c. Parent/base e584ad6, exact six paths, diff-check clean, no media blob, and the raw-video/edition/timebase/diagnostic/anti-circularity distinctions are sound. The blocker is recall-human-source scope. The candidate says participant recall transcripts/exports may be committed and shared and that no Sherlock-specific consent/REB/participant-prose hold applies (court lines 21-24, 37-39, 142-147, 187-196; plan lines 563-569; source audit lines 228-238, 274-276). Yet it simultaneously says Constitution IX is not amended, while Constitution IX says redistribution and remote processing of participant text are governed by consent and REB approval, and the binding story-text checklist lines 48-56 bars participant recall text until an owner-recorded REB/IRB redistribution basis appears in the admitted file header. The owner's stated local scientific-use/no-raw-video-Git direction removes a BBC episode-licence blocker for local processing; it is not itself a recorded participant-data redistribution basis. Successor must separate (a) local scientific use of episode/video and locally held recall data, authorized for this vertical, from (b) Git/public redistribution of participant recall prose. Keep raw video external; keep participant recall prose external/no-Git unless and until the existing checklist's per-artifact REB/IRB basis is recorded; allow non-text derived graphs/features/reports and annotations only through their applicable admissions. Do not reinstate a BBC-permission gate or block local Sherlock work. Add a counterfactual court: local-use authorization true + participant-redistribution basis absent => vertical may run locally but recall prose cannot enter Git/shareable bundle. This is the requested recall/admission-policy review, not a legal adjudication or landing action.
